segments.title: Chương 119: Các Nhân Viên Mới Của Công Ty
segments.content:
Chapter 122: The Company's New Employees

Chen Guiliang and Wu Meng had already eaten dinner, so they only picked at a few dishes.

After gobbling down his food for a while, Xie Yang felt a little embarrassed, as if he were a refugee who had fled a famine to seek refuge with relatives.

To save money, this fellow had bought a hard-seat ticket from Hangzhou to Beijing and had only eaten a few bags of instant noodles along the way.

"I'm almost full," Xie Yang said, slowing his chewing.

Chen Guiliang said, "Would we laugh at you for that? We all trained for this in the cafeteria during the second semester of our senior year. I usually just swallow without chewing like that too."

Xie Yang knew Chen Guiliang was trying to save him face, and suddenly he felt a little like crying. He didn't know how he had ended up in this state.

"If I could live my life over, I would definitely study hard in my senior year," Xie Yang said with a sigh.

Chen Guiliang said, "Actually, it's not too late to start studying now."

He knew how capable Xie Yang was.

In the other timeline, Xie Yang had been spurred into action during his freshman year, tutoring to earn extra money while burying his head in books to study hard. In the end, he got into a pretty damn good university for his master's degree.

Wu Meng also said, "Yeah, you can also audit classes here at Peking University. Great Hero Chen's Yuanpei Program got the course schedules for the entire university right at the start of the semester. If there's any class you want to audit, you can have Great Hero Chen help you keep an eye out for the classroom."

"Won't I get kicked out?" Xie Yang asked.

Wu Meng smiled, "Peking University has so many students, who can recognize them all? As long as you don't say anything, nobody will know your situation."

Xie Yang said, "I'll give it a try then."

The three of them chatted about amusing high school stories for a while longer, then Chen Guiliang went to pay the bill.

Wu Meng went straight back to the university through the south gate, while Chen Guiliang took Xie Yang west, walking around the southwest corner of the campus towards Changchun New Garden.

Pointing at a dormitory building, Chen Guiliang explained, "This is a new dormitory complex at Peking University that was just completed this year. Buildings 1 and 2 are all master's and doctoral students."

"Buildings 3 and 4 are for young teachers, visiting scholars, and entrepreneurs from the science park. In principle, regular employees can't live here. But there are a lot of empty rooms right now, so you can stay here temporarily. You'll probably have to move out when the fall semester starts next year. You can find another place to live then."

"Our company is near the east gate, and the Changchun New Garden dorms are near the west gate. You can cut across the Peking University campus to get to and from work, or you can go around from the north or south side."

A light snow was still falling.

Xie Yang looked around as he walked, never having imagined that he would one day be able to live in a Peking University dorm.

Chen Guiliang led him to the management center of Changchun New Garden, registered him in the company's name, and then paid for a mattress, quilt, and other supplies.

Next, he took Xie Yang to Building 4, knocked on a door, and made the introductions, "This is Ding Qiang and Cai Yifei, our colleagues from the company. This is my friend, Xie Yang, your new roommate. He's also going to join the company."

Ding Qiang had a vocational college degree, and Cai Yifei had graduated from a Tier 2 university. Both were full-time programmers.

"Hello."

"Hello, come on in."

Chen Guiliang walked into the dorm room and took a look around, grumbling, "Damn, the conditions here are great, way better than my shabby dorm. I kind of want to move in here myself!"

Ding Qiang stood there, not daring to reply.

Cai Yifei was more outgoing and even dared to joke with the boss, "Then why don't you move in?"

"It's too far," Chen Guiliang shook his head. "It's inconvenient for work and class."

This was, of course, just a casual remark. The dorm was only 300 meters from the west gate of Peking University; it couldn't be considered far by any means.

Chen Guiliang sat for a little while longer before taking his leave, "You guys get to know each other. I have to hurry back to my dorm, or I'll be marked down for being late."

The three of them saw him to the door.

Ding Qiang silently helped Xie Yang make his bed.

Cai Yifei, however, offered Xie Yang a cigarette and asked, "What's your position at the company?"

"I don't know," Xie Yang said. "I might have to do odd jobs at first and learn a few things from everyone. I want to learn programming."

Cai Yifei took out a lighter and lit the cigarette for him. "Have you learned programming before?"

Xie Yang replied, "I've only been teaching myself for a few months, with some guidance from an expert. I've just gotten started with Java and C."

Ding Qiang, who had been making the bed, said encouragingly, "It's okay, I'm also learning from an expert. We can make progress together in the future."

"Thanks." Xie Yang felt that Ding Qiang seemed like a nice guy.

Cai Yifei started to inquire, "You and Boss Chen are from the same hometown?"

Xie Yang wasn't used to the title "Boss Chen" yet and subconsciously asked, "You mean Chen Guiliang?"

"Yes," Cai Yifei nodded.

Xie Yang said, "We were high school classmates."

"I hear Boss Chen was a big deal in high school?" Cai Yifei asked curiously.

Xie Yang said with a smile, "He's exceptionally awesome. Let me tell you... um, he's just very diligent and hardworking."

Xie Yang stopped himself halfway through.

He felt he shouldn't be casually telling a colleague about Chen Guiliang's past.

At critical moments, Xie Yang's lips were always sealed. To this day, he had never told anyone that Chen Guiliang had run a private game server.

This guy was actually more suited for administrative work. But he insisted on learning programming, only because he thought programming was awesome and had a very promising future.

The next day.

Ding Qiang and Cai Yifei each left on a bicycle.

Xie Yang sat on the back of Ding Qiang's.

But it was Cai Yifei who was making the introductions along the way, "Outside the south gate of Peking University, you can get a secondhand bicycle. You can go buy one too. We eat at the science park building's cafeteria. It's more expensive than the cafeterias on campus, but cheaper than the restaurants outside."

"I'll go buy one this weekend then," Xie Yang said.

Cai Yifei smiled, "I'll take you, I know where the cheapest ones are. When the company isn't busy, we can ride around. Maybe we'll run into a pretty girl on the Peking University campus."

They arrived at the building's cafeteria.

Cai Yifei bought a bowl of beef noodles and added an egg.

Ding Qiang only had two steamed buns and some congee.

Cai Yifei couldn't help but say, "You're so frugal every day, can your body take it?"

Ding Qiang said, "I've eaten like this since I was a kid."

Cai Yifei said to Xie Yang, "It's a good thing you moved into the dorm, otherwise I'd have no one to talk to. Our Brother Ding is a real clam. You can't even joke with him. I'm about to get an internal injury from being so bottled up."

Xie Yang said, "Why don't you find a girlfriend?"

Cai Yifei sighed while peeling his egg, "Just broke up. If it weren't for her, I wouldn't have even stayed in Beijing. We worked at the same company, and she had the nerve to cheat on me right under my nose. And it was with my goddamn supervisor!"

"That is pretty ballsy," Xie Yang commented.

Cai Yifei gave a bitter, self-mocking smile, "I beat the crap out of my supervisor, got detained for a few days, and when I got out, my job was gone. I just bought a recruitment newspaper, followed an address, and ended up in Boss Chen's company. I guess you could call it fate."

Right after, Cai Yifei started ranting about what an idiot his former supervisor was.

Ding Qiang listened silently, while Xie Yang chimed in with a few words now and then.

Before they had finished their meal, two female colleagues arrived. They were customer service staff and general hands that Chen Guiliang had hired.

As final exams drew nearer, all the part-time Peking University students at the company had left.

"This is Zhu Xia and Gong Xiaozhen..." Cai Yifei helped with the introductions.

Gong Xiaozhen was quite pretty. Xie Yang couldn't help but flick his hair.

Compared to his senior year of high school, Xie Yang was a bit more handsome now—he had less acne.

Gong Xiaozhen's attention, however, was on Cai Yifei.

Because Cai Yifei was a graduate from a Tier 2 university, handsome, had a higher salary, and a more promising future.

Unfortunately, the lady was willing, but the gentleman was not.

Cai Yifei even found the two girls too slow at eating and couldn't be bothered to wait for them. He took Xie Yang and headed upstairs to the company.

"Both of these companies belong to Boss Chen," Cai Yifei explained. "They're pretty much like one company, and the employees are shared between them. If one side gets too busy, they'll ask someone from the other side to come and lend a hand. The head manager is Ao Yanchen. She's Boss Chen's senior, and she manages both companies by herself."

Looking at the two company offices, each occupying 50 square meters, Xie Yang felt extremely shocked—this was much more tangible than a website or a game.

His old roommate had achieved all this in just half a year, while his only progress had been learning a little programming.

Cai Yifei took Xie Yang to meet the other colleagues, while Ding Qiang went directly to his own workstation.

It was mid-morning when Ao Yanchen finally arrived, late. She had come over after attending one of her major courses.

Ao Yanchen called Xie Yang outside, "You'll be an intern at the company first. The intern salary is 1200. Don't tell the other colleagues the specific amount. During your internship, your duties won't be fixed. You can learn whatever you're interested in. Of course, if the company is short-staffed somewhere, you'll be asked to help out too."

"I understand. Thank you, Supervisor... Ao." Xie Yang was quite embarrassed.

With his current education and abilities, there was no way he could get an internship salary of 1200. It was purely a favor for an old classmate.

Xie Yang's first job was to promote *Sanguosha* on forums and Tieba... he felt like he was back in the days of promoting private game servers with Chen Guiliang.

Just before noon, Chen Guiliang finally showed up.

Li Xunhuan came too. He looked around the two offices and said, "This is set up pretty well. The offices are quite spacious."

Chen Guiliang smiled, "The rent is cheap, so I'm just setting up the framework first."

"How many users does your online *Sanguosha* have?" Li Xunhuan asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Over 7,000 registered accounts, mostly students from major universities in Beijing, directed from the campus network. Last weekend, the peak concurrent users were over 2,300."

"That's not a lot," Li Xunhuan said.

Chen Guiliang explained, "The ad space on 17173.com is too expensive, so I couldn't bring myself to buy it. But I'm already promoting it on forums and Tieba. I also include the official *Sanguosha* website at the end of every chapter when I update *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* on my blog and forums. The user growth rate these past two days has been pretty good, especially from the board game Tieba. Although it's not a huge community, the entire Tieba has basically migrated over. At the current growth rate, *Sanguosha*'s user count will definitely break 15,000 before the end of the month."

"I still think it's too much effort," Li Xunhuan shook his head.

Chen Guiliang wanted him to be the agent for the physical card version of *Sanguosha*.

This kind of product was considered a publication and should have been handed over to a publishing company to act as an agent. In the other timeline, the agent for the physical *Sanguosha* cards was indeed a publishing company.

But Li Xunhuan found it troublesome and felt that *Sanguosha* wasn't famous enough yet, requiring a great deal of effort to promote.

Chen Guiliang said, "If Boss Lu isn't interested, then forget it. I'll find other publishers. How are things going with *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty*?"

"I'm just waiting for your manuscript. Hurry up and get enough of it together," Li Xunhuan said. "I've taken the media reports and online data to contact various book distribution channels, and they all think this book has a promising future."

Li Xunhuan had many more marketing tricks up his sleeve.

He had already made a deal with Dangdang.com for an exclusive pre-sale of *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty*, and in return, Dangdang.com was willing to provide ample publicity.

To secure distribution through Xinhua Bookstore, he even increased the supply discount, getting Xinhua Bookstore to agree to set up a "bestseller section." This would allow consumers to immediately see *Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty* as soon as they entered a Xinhua Bookstore.

Giving Chen Guiliang a high royalty share and Xinhua Bookstore a high supply discount, could Li Xunhuan still make a profit?

If sales were high, he would.

If sales were low, he would suffer a huge loss!

(End of Chapter)
